title: Exact Power of Three
statement:
You get a 32-bit signed integer n. Return true if n equals 3^k for some whole number k ≥ 0, and false otherwise.

Note that 3^0 = 1 counts.

examples.why: 45 is divisible by 3, and so is 15, but then 5 is not. Being divisible by 3 is not enough.
Powers of three with k ≥ 0 are always positive.

hints: If n is a power of three, what happens when you keep dividing it by 3?
Divide by 3 while the remainder is 0. A power of three ends at exactly 1. Handle n ≤ 0 first.
No loop: the largest power of three that fits in 32 bits is 3^19 = 1162261467. Its only divisors are smaller powers of three, so n > 0 is a power of three exactly when 1162261467 % n === 0.

explain.intuition:
A power of three is 1 multiplied by 3 again and again. So undo that: divide by 3 while it divides evenly, and see whether you land on 1. Anything else, like the 5 left over from 45, means another prime factor was hiding inside.

There is a neat shortcut because 3 is prime. The biggest 32-bit power of three, 3^19 = 1162261467, has only powers of three as divisors. So a positive n divides it exactly when n is itself a power of three. This trick needs a prime base: it would not work for powers of 4.
pitfalls: Forgetting n = 0: 0 % 3 === 0 forever, so the loop never ends.
Using Math.log(n) / Math.log(3) and checking for a whole number. Floating-point error makes results like 4.999999 for 243.
Returning true for any multiple of 3, like 45.

solutions.title: Divide down to one
solutions.idea: Strip factors of 3 while they divide evenly. Only a power of three reaches exactly 1.

solutions.title: Divisor of the largest power
solutions.idea: 3^19 is the largest power of three in 32 bits. Because 3 is prime, its positive divisors are exactly the powers of three up to it.

followups: Why does the divisor trick fail for powers of 4? What would you do instead?
Check a power of three without any loop and without the magic constant, using base-3 conversion.
